/-!
# Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture

The Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture (1972) is a problem about coloring unions of cliques. It says:
if $k$ complete graphs, each having exactly $k$ vertices, have the property that every pair of
complete graphs has at most one shared vertex, then the union of the graphs can be properly
colored with $k$ colors.

Kang, Kelly, Kühn, Methuku and Osthus proved the conjecture for all sufficiently large $k$.
The conjecture for every $k$ remains open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Faber%E2%80%93Lov%C3%A1sz_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- D. Y. Kang, T. Kelly, D. Kühn, A. Methuku, D. Osthus,
  *A proof of the Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture*, Ann. of Math. (2) 198 (2023), 537–618.
  [arXiv:2101.04698](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04698)
-/

lemma iSup_spanningCoe_completeGraph_adj {V : Type*} {k : ℕ} (C : Fin k → Finset V) (u v : V) :
    (⨆ i, (completeGraph (C i : Set V)).spanningCoe).Adj u v ↔
      u ≠ v ∧ ∃ i, u ∈ C i ∧ v ∈ C i := by
  simp only [iSup_adj, spanningCoe, map_adj, completeGraph, top_adj, ne_eq,
    Function.Embedding.coe_subtype]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨i, ⟨a, ha⟩, ⟨b, hb⟩, hab, rfl, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨fun h => hab (Subtype.ext h), i, by simpa using ha, by simpa using hb⟩
  · rintro ⟨hne, i, hu, hv⟩
    exact ⟨i, ⟨u, by simpa using hu⟩, ⟨v, by simpa using hv⟩,
      fun h => hne (congrArg Subtype.val h), rfl, rfl⟩

    (hinter : Pairwise fun i j => (C i ∩ C j).card ≤ 1)

blocks.docstring:
**Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture.**
If $k$ complete graphs, each having exactly $k$ vertices, have the property that every pair of
complete graphs has at most one shared vertex, then the union of the graphs can be properly
colored with $k$ colors.

Here the $i$-th complete graph has vertex set `C i`, so its edges are all pairs of distinct
vertices of `C i`, and the union of the graphs is `⨆ i, (completeGraph (C i : Set V)).spanningCoe`.
The vertex set of this union is the union of the `C i`, so the hypothesis `hcover` says that the
vertex type `V` is exactly this vertex set. The conclusion `Colorable k` says that this graph has
a proper coloring with $k$ colors.

claims.decomposer_note: The statement only names the conjecture ('on coloring unions of cliques'), so the precise Prop is taken from the article: for every k, any graph that is the union of k cliques (complete graphs on k-element vertex sets, Wikipedia says exactly k vertices while KKKMO's equivalent form allows at most k) with pairwise intersections of size ≤ 1 has chromatic number ≤ k; the article's committee, linear-hypergraph chromatic-index, intersection-graph and linear-intersection-number formulations are stated as equivalent reformulations of this same question rather than distinct questions, and the partial results (3k/2−2, k+o(k), large k, fractional, L ≤ 10) and the unrestricted-intersection 'related problem' are not posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: c04 states the Wikipedia lead sentence most literally: the k complete graphs are `completeGraph (C i : Set V)` for `C : Fin k → Finset V` with `(C i).card = k`, their union is the lattice supremum `⨆ i, (·).spanningCoe : SimpleGraph V`, pairwise intersections `≤ 1` via `Pairwise` (i ≠ j only), and the conclusion is Mathlib's `Colorable k`. `hcover` fixes V to be exactly the union's vertex set, which matches 'the union of the graphs' and makes k = 0 correct. I verified by a scratch proof that the adjacency is `u ≠ v ∧ ∃ i, u ∈ C i ∧ v ∈ C i` and shipped that as an `@[category API]` lemma alongside the theorem. Docstring/module header composed from c04 and c06/c07. All other candidates (c01–c03, c05–c08) are also faithful; c01/c03/c08 avoid SimpleGraph (coloring injective on each clique), c05 restricts V to Fin n, c02 introduces a bespoke `unionOfCliques` def, c06/c07 use `fromRel` — all equivalent, just less literal or less idiomatic.

/-!
# Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture

The Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture (1972) is a problem about coloring unions of cliques. It says:
if $k$ complete graphs, each having exactly $k$ vertices, have the property that every pair of
complete graphs has at most one shared vertex, then the union of the graphs can be properly
colored with $k$ colors.

Kang, Kelly, Kühn, Methuku and Osthus proved the conjecture for all sufficiently large $k$.
The conjecture for every $k$ remains open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Faber%E2%80%93Lov%C3%A1sz_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- D. Y. Kang, T. Kelly, D. Kühn, A. Methuku, D. Osthus,
  *A proof of the Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture*, Ann. of Math. (2) 198 (2023), 537–618.
  [arXiv:2101.04698](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04698)

namespace ErdosFaberLovaszConjecture

open SimpleGraph

/--
Two vertices are adjacent in the union of the complete graphs on the vertex sets `C i` if and
only if they are distinct and both lie in some `C i`.
-/
@[category API, AMS 5]
lemma iSup_spanningCoe_completeGraph_adj {V : Type*} {k : ℕ} (C : Fin k → Finset V) (u v : V) :
    (⨆ i, (completeGraph (C i : Set V)).spanningCoe).Adj u v ↔
      u ≠ v ∧ ∃ i, u ∈ C i ∧ v ∈ C i := by
  simp only [iSup_adj, spanningCoe, map_adj, completeGraph, top_adj, ne_eq,
    Function.Embedding.coe_subtype]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨i, ⟨a, ha⟩, ⟨b, hb⟩, hab, rfl, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨fun h => hab (Subtype.ext h), i, by simpa using ha, by simpa using hb⟩
  · rintro ⟨hne, i, hu, hv⟩
    exact ⟨i, ⟨u, by simpa using hu⟩, ⟨v, by simpa using hv⟩,
      fun h => hne (congrArg Subtype.val h), rfl, rfl⟩

/--
**Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture.**
If $k$ complete graphs, each having exactly $k$ vertices, have the property that every pair of
complete graphs has at most one shared vertex, then the union of the graphs can be properly
colored with $k$ colors.

Here the $i$-th complete graph has vertex set `C i`, so its edges are all pairs of distinct
vertices of `C i`, and the union of the graphs is `⨆ i, (completeGraph (C i : Set V)).spanningCoe`.
The vertex set of this union is the union of the `C i`, so the hypothesis `hcover` says that the
vertex type `V` is exactly this vertex set. The conclusion `Colorable k` says that this graph has
a proper coloring with $k$ colors.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_faber_lovasz_conjecture {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (k : ℕ) (C : Fin k → Finset V)
    (hcard : ∀ i, (C i).card = k)
    (hinter : Pairwise fun i j => (C i ∩ C j).card ≤ 1)
    (hcover : ∀ v, ∃ i, v ∈ C i) :
    (⨆ i, (completeGraph (C i : Set V)).spanningCoe).Colorable k := by
  sorry

end ErdosFaberLovaszConjecture

items: Precise formulation taken from the article's lead sentence (the list entry only names the conjecture): k complete graphs on exactly k vertices each, pairwise sharing at most one vertex, union is k-colorable. The 'exactly k vertices' reading of Wikipedia is used, not KKKMO's 'at most k' variant.

Cliques are represented by their vertex sets `C : Fin k → Finset V` (indexed by Fin k, so there are exactly k of them, possibly with repetition; for k ≥ 2 the intersection hypothesis forces them to be distinct, and for k ≤ 1 repetition is harmless). The i-th complete graph is `(completeGraph (C i : Set V)).spanningCoe`, and the union is the lattice supremum `⨆ i` in `SimpleGraph V`. I verified in a scratch file that its adjacency is `u ≠ v ∧ ∃ i, u ∈ C i ∧ v ∈ C i`.

The hypothesis `hcover : ∀ v, ∃ i, v ∈ C i` makes the vertex type V exactly the vertex set of the union of the cliques (as in the informal statement, where 'the union of the graphs' has vertex set ⋃ C i). Without it, the statement would be false in the degenerate case k = 0 with V nonempty (the empty graph on a nonempty type is not 0-colorable), while for k ≥ 1 it is equivalent to the version without hcover (isolated vertices do not affect k-colorability). hcover also makes V finite automatically.

'Every pair of complete graphs has at most one shared vertex' is `Pairwise fun i j => (C i ∩ C j).card ≤ 1`, i.e. only for i ≠ j; `[DecidableEq V]` is assumed only so that Finset intersection is available.
Conclusion is `Colorable k` (existence of a proper coloring with colors in Fin k) rather than `chromaticNumber ≤ k`; these are equivalent by `SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber_le_iff_colorable`.

Category `research open` as required by the task status, although the article notes the conjecture was proved for all sufficiently large k by Kang–Kelly–Kühn–Methuku–Osthus (the full conjecture for all k remains open).

reviewer_notes: Original list entry only names the conjecture; the Prop is taken from the article lead ('exactly k vertices'), which is equivalent to KKKMO's 'at most k' form. Indexing by Fin k permits repeated vertex sets in principle, but for k ≥ 2 a repeat violates the intersection bound and for k ≤ 1 it is immaterial. `Colorable k` = 'at most k colors' = chromatic number ≤ k, the standard reading of 'can be properly colored with k colors'. Category left as `research open` per the given status (the conjecture is proved only for all sufficiently large k). No candidate omitted the slot; there were no decomposition objections.
